text:
maya: Quick sync — after the Friday deploy we've got a mix of customer P0s and a handful of UX asks. Need to decide hotpatch vs next 2-week wave.
liam: Logs look like a memory leak in the KV cache. Repro rate ~4% but spikes under burst. I’m +hotfix.
ashley: Customer PM asked for the UX list (session restore flow) — high MRR customers want it. Not sure if it needs immediate attention.
carlos: Support: two customers hit failures (one dedicated) and one reported increased tail latency. They’re blocking live demos tomorrow.
jen: Design: the session restore polish is mostly visual and can be toggled behind a flag. Not a P0 IMO.
raj: SRE: if we can ship a small rollback or canary tonight we can stop the error ramp. Canary + monitor for 2 hours should be fine.
maya: Proposal: triage items into 3 buckets — Hotpatch (safety/regression), Urgent follow-on (customer-impact but non-crash), Backlog (polish).
maya: Short checklist I’m using: 1) Is user-facing outage? 2) Does it affect MRR/customers live? 3) Can we patch in <8 dev-hours? 4) Rollback risk.
liam: Based on that the KV leak = Hotpatch. I can scope a minimal fix + test. Needs eng pair for QA.
naya: (oops wrong channel)
ashley: So UX polish -> Backlog unless a paying customer escalates. We can ship behind flag in next wave.
carlos: +1 to hotpatch. Customers asked for ETA — can we commit to a morning patch?
liam: I can get a PR ready by EOD. Need QA signoff — @jen or @raj to help with canary criteria.
jen: I’ll prepare a short checklist for QA and a mock for the rollback flag.
raj: I’ll run a canary tonight 10pm UTC if deploy-bot approves. Need the deploy window and runbook entry.
maya: Action items: 1) liam PR by EOD, 2) jen QA checklist, 3) raj runbook + canary window, 4) ashley update customers about plan. I’ll update the triage sheet: https://docs.internal/redwood/triage-queue (please add notes).
liam: If hotpatch lands cleanly we still want to reserve 30% band for urgent follow-ons in next sprint so we don’t block roadmap.
maya: Agreed — sprint plan: next 2 weeks = 60% new-wave, 30% follow-ons/higher priority bugs, 10% spikes/hotfix carryover.
ashley: Can we add a quick measurement to ensure perf doesn't regress after hotfix? token/p95 latency dashboard?
raj: Adding an alert rule: p95 latency > baseline + 15% during canary -> auto-rollback.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary window 2029-07-15T22:00Z, watchers: raj, liam, jen.
carlos: I’ll tell the customers we expect a canary tonight and a follow-up by morning.
maya: Thanks — will reconvene after canary and then finalize sprint slice. If canary fails we do rollback + blameless postmortem. :thumbsup:
